Max size: 40 cm SL. The spotted steed, Hemibarbus maculatus, is a cyprinid widespread in eastern Asia between the Yangtze and Amur basins, including Taiwan and Hainan. It has 7–11 large blackish spots on each flank and a deep body with a clearly convex dorsal profile. A riverine fish of clear, well-oxygenated running water, it breeds in May and June, depositing its eggs among aquatic vegetation. It has probably been introduced to Vietnam and Laos, or records from there represent another species.

Needs a very large tank and should be kept in a group.

Widespread in eastern Asia between the Yangtze and Amur river basins, including China (mainland and the islands of Taiwan and Hainan), Korea, Mongolia, Russia and Japan. It has probably been introduced to Vietnam and Laos, or records from these countries represent another species.

Type locality is 'Chang Jiang [Yangtze River], China'.
Predominantly a riverine fish preferring clear, well-oxygenated, running waters with substrates of sand, gravel, rock or mud.
Wild individuals are known to feed on benthic crustaceans, insects and molluscs.
In nature it breeds between May and June, with eggs deposited among aquatic vegetation.

This species can be distinguished from other members of the genus by the following combination of characters: 7–11 large blackish spots on each flank; body deep with clearly convex dorsal profile; head length shorter than body depth; snout length shorter than or equal to postorbital head length; lips not developed, lateral lobes of lower lip narrow, without folds, the median process large and marked; barbel length ½–⅔ of eye diameter; dorsal spine strong, equal to HL, last simple ray ossified and thicker than branched rays; origin of dorsal fin closer to tip of snout than caudal-fin base; 6½ branched anal-fin rays.
